record.original_question: For material particles moving in R^d with d>1 that stick on collision, can one find a variational description that covers both potential and non-potential fluid flows and is flexible enough to model formation and evolution of shock waves for the multidimensional Burgers equation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider material particles moving in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d>1$ which interact by perfectly inelastic collisions: when two or more particles meet, they merge into a single particle whose mass is the sum of the colliding masses and whose momentum is the sum of the colliding momenta (the "sticky particle" rule). The macroscopic limit of such dynamics is expected to describe pressureless gas dynamics and, in particular, the formation and evolution of shocks in the multidimensional inviscid Burgers equation
$$\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v = 0, \qquad v:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d.$$
For potential initial velocity fields $v_0=\nabla\varphi_0$, the solution before shocks can be obtained from the Hopf–Lax variational principle, and the sticky particle dynamics admits a variational characterization (as a gradient/Wasserstein-type flow in the space of measures). However, this potential framework does not apply to general, non-potential initial velocity fields in dimension $d>1$.

Problem. Construct a variational principle (an action functional, minimization, or equivalent variational characterization on a suitable space of mass distributions and velocity fields) for the sticky-particle dynamics in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d>1$, that:
(i) describes both potential and non-potential fluid flows in a unified manner;
(ii) is sufficiently flexible to model the formation and subsequent evolution of shock waves for the multidimensional inviscid Burgers equation.
artifact.category_tag: Sticky particle dynamics and Burgers shocks
artifact.status_search_result: A variational/Wasserstein description of sticky-particle dynamics is well-developed in the potential (one-dimensional, or gradient) case, and connections between multidimensional Burgers shocks and the geometry of diffeomorphism groups / Wasserstein space have been studied (e.g., Khesin–Misiolek). However, no unified variational framework covering both potential and non-potential flows in dimension $d>1$ that flexibly models multidimensional Burgers shock formation appears to have been established; the problem is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Shock waves for the Burgers equation and curvatures of diffeomorphism groups
status_evidence.snippet: Shock formation in multidimensional Burgers corresponds to a focal/conjugate point along a geodesic in the Wasserstein space of densities.
status_evidence.claim: Geometric/Wasserstein interpretations exist but the unified variational sticky-particle framework in d>1 is not established.

status_evidence.title: Systems of Sticky Particles Governed by Burgers' Equation
status_evidence.snippet: The entropy solution of the inviscid Burgers' equation is interpreted as the velocity function of a sticky particles model, shown only for continuous initial data; the connection with trajectories is still unknown.
status_evidence.claim: Even in simpler settings, the full sticky-particle/Burgers correspondence has unresolved aspects.
